system.summary: Polyphonic substitution: each digit 1-9 stands for two letters, 0 is a null, with four-digit X0Y0 and dotted two-digit nomenclator codes.

prior_solution.where: George Lasry's reconstructed key (24 Oct 2020) is attached to every record R85-R90; no plaintext posted. Serrano, Correspondencia diplomatica (1914) may print some of these letters in clear; not checked (HathiTrust blocked).

conditions.human_role: Set the target; supplied nothing further. DECODE reached with a cookie already in the repository.

solution.what: Fetched DECODE records R85-R90, their transcriptions and key files, and two page images, with the repository cookie.
Found Lasry's reconstructed key on every record, byte-identical to the key on R93-R102 (alessandrino1568); no plaintext attached.
Identified sender, recipient and year from the archive description on the records (ff. 146-338 = Alessandrino to the nuncio, 1567) and the clear openings on ff. 163r, 299r.
Tried archive.org and HathiTrust for Serrano 1914; not on archive.org, HathiTrust 403.
Ran the alessandrino1568 decoder unchanged on the six transcriptions.

All six read as continuous Italian: Philip II's journey to Flanders and a papal interview, Borromeo's Milan jurisdiction, the archbishop of Cologne, the second French civil war; R88/R89 are two copies of one letter and R90 repeats its close.

Historical consistency: Morvilliers, l'Aubespine, Montmorency, Conde and Coligny in arms date R88-R90 to Oct-Nov 1567; Cologne (von Wied, unconfirmed) and the Milan dispute fit 1567; the two copies R88/R89 agree.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): DECODE transcriptions (RebAn 2016) per record; decryptions = the word-split DECODE bodies from decode_updates/decryptions copied into texts/, plus decrypt_raw.txt, all with Lasry's key as filed (decode/DOC_R85_D3265_3265.txt etc.).

Reading audit (George Lasry's test: can a reader build coherent sentences and translate them?). texts/R85-R90_decryption.txt and decrypt_raw.txt read: Italian fragments between garbled strings in nearly every line in all six letters (R85, R87, R89 closely), e.g. 'pur tu giudica che saria bene che re inuita sectabolo oposi satisfatione del mondosi'; docs/_check_reading.py 21-40% of sentences clean in the word-split files. All six relabelled decoded, not read; class read -> not read, method read with known key -> not solved (key kept as a part); fraction_read unknown -> 0.

outcome.method_basis: Lasry's reconstructed key, attached to every DECODE record R85-R90, applied through the alessandrino1568 polyphonic decoder with an Italian LM (read with known key, recorded under parts), gives Italian fragments with garbled strings in nearly every line; no letter builds sentences.
outcome.notes: Machine output under a polyphonic key: letters are model choices, so isolated letters, the recurring group 'colospo' and unlisted dotted groups ([NN.]) are uncertain; the sense is continuous throughout. Not checked against Serrano.

credits.note: reconstructed key on DECODE R85-R90 (24 Oct 2020), identical to the R93-R102 key, applied unchanged

texts.label: R85, Spagna 1 item 1, f. 165r [1567]
texts.summary: Cardinal Alessandrino (Michele Bonelli) to the nuncio at Madrid, Giovan Battista Castagna, 1567: the Pope wishes to be certain whether the King's journey to Flanders will take place, because he then wants an interview (abboccamento) with him, and the nuncio is to find out and exhort the King.
texts.note: Word-split decoder output with Lasry's polyphonic key on DECODE's transcription: Italian fragments ('nostro signore', 'tumulti di francia', 'sua santita') between garbled strings in nearly every line ('rimpesti e beuersi', 'allcgcatolica li a [?] ltra piu banden gato'); no sentence can be built (reading audit, 22 Oct 2026).

texts.label: R86, Spagna 1 item 2, f. 236r [1567]
texts.summary: Milan: the proceedings against the authors of the outrage on the jurisdiction of the archbishop (Borromeo). The Pope will use spiritual arms and a monitorium; the dignity of the Holy See requires proceeding at least against the Capitano di giustizia, the fiscal and some of the Senate, and the King should deprive his ministers concerned.
texts.note: Word-split decoder output with Lasry's polyphonic key on DECODE's transcription: Italian fragments ('nostro signore', 'tumulti di francia', 'sua santita') between garbled strings in nearly every line ('rimpesti e beuersi', 'allcgcatolica li a [?] ltra piu banden gato'); no sentence can be built (reading audit, 22 Oct 2026).

texts.label: R87, Spagna 1 item 3, ff. 249r-250r [1567]
texts.summary: The Pope wants the King's journey to Flanders, for the restoration of religion there and in Germany. The archbishop of Cologne (Friedrich von Wied) has not sought confirmation nor made the Tridentine profession of faith; the Pope means to proceed to his deprivation, and the King should work so that the Cologne chapter does not designate a suspect successor.
texts.note: Word-split decoder output with Lasry's polyphonic key on DECODE's transcription: Italian fragments ('nostro signore', 'tumulti di francia', 'sua santita') between garbled strings in nearly every line ('rimpesti e beuersi', 'allcgcatolica li a [?] ltra piu banden gato'); no sentence can be built (reading audit, 22 Oct 2026).

texts.label: R88, Spagna 1 item 4, f. 301r-v [autumn 1567]
texts.summary: On the troubles of France (the second civil war): the King of France trusts the Chancellor, Morvilliers and l'Aubespine too much, the Queen Mother's ambition keeps the kingdom divided, and if the Constable Montmorency and his son were imprisoned until the Admiral and the Prince laid down their arms, an end would soon be put to the troubles. One of two copies of the letter (with R89).
